supporting_observations.claim: The provided process-creation records do not show PowerShell at the reported time around 13:40 UTC; they show WmiPrvSE starting at 13:39:51, followed by system authentication and directory-service activity. This does not rule out an unrecorded or otherwise unobserved PowerShell launch.

At 13:45:45, PowerShell ran on WS-JFROST-01 as ali.hassan with the command to run the known workstation patch script from FILE-MAP-01. This is consistent with the stated IT practice and scheduled workstation patching, but occurs several minutes after the reported appearance.
The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update and then exited shortly afterward, consistent with the patching command’s purpose.

At 14:04:14, Explorer updated Julia Frost’s UserAssist entry for the PowerShell executable. This supports that PowerShell was recorded as launched under her profile at some point, but the record does not establish the launch time, command line, or purpose.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied evidence includes process-creation records but no PowerShell script-block or module logging, console contents, or evidence linking the reported window to a particular process. The later PowerShell process is recorded at 13:45:45, not around 13:40 (T164-00280, T164-00281).
The UserAssist entry is a registry update, not a process-creation record; it does not identify the command or prove what was displayed in the reported window (T164-00343).
The available logs do not establish whether a PowerShell process occurred around 13:40 but was not captured.
claims_not_established: Whether Julia Frost actually saw a PowerShell window around 13:40 UTC, and which process or user session caused it.
Whether the PowerShell launch reflected in UserAssist at 14:04:14 was interactive, what command it ran, or whether it is related to the reported window.
Whether any unrecorded PowerShell activity occurred around 13:40.
additional_evidence_needed: Endpoint process and console/session telemetry for WS-JFROST-01 covering the reported time, including process ancestry and any PowerShell host or terminal events.
PowerShell operational, script-block, and module logs, if enabled, for WS-JFROST-01 during the review window.
Clarification from Julia about the precise time and what was visible, and confirmation from IT whether the observed patch run accounts for the report.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: records show a Kerberos request for noah.kim and a network logon to WS-NKIM-01 originating from WS-JFROST-01’s address. This is not evidence about the alerted PowerShell activity (T164-00127, T164-00128, T164-00130).
Separate review: a domain credential validation for greta.lund lists WS-JFROST-01 as the workstation; the supplied record alone does not establish a successful logon or its purpose (T164-00316).

Separate review: Julia’s browser accessed Google Drive and Dropbox, services not listed as approved in the supplied environment context. The records show page or resource requests, not that files were uploaded or exfiltrated (T164-00443, T164-00470, T164-00626, T164-00627).
